name: damage-overflow-saturate
summary: Huge damage wraps to a negative and then clamps to 1. Saturate at a maximum instead.
status: BUILT AND STATICALLY VERIFIED -- not yet run by a zone process.
why: RulesOfEngagement::roe_CalcDamage (0x505C00) returns int, but the damage pipeline underneath it
(roe_Damage and friends) works in DOUBLE. The conversion is a single call:
0x506187   call __ftol2_sse      ; (int)damage
__ftol2_sse returns the x86 'integer indefinite' 0x80000000 when the double does not fit in an
int32 -- that is the huge negative. It then survives three modifiers (two vtable calls and
roe_LevelGapDamageRevision, all of which keep it negative) and reaches the tail:
0x5061C9   test eax, eax
0x5061CB   jg   ok
0x5061CD   mov  dword ptr [ebp-0x10], 1     ; <-- the clamp to 1
so the biggest hit in the game lands for 1.
WHY NOT JUST CHANGE THE CLAMP. That '1' is also the floor for legitimately non-positive damage --
defence at or above attack. Rewriting it to a maximum would make every weak hit a maximum hit. By
the time execution reaches the clamp the magnitude is already gone; the fix has to be at the
conversion, which is the last place that knows the difference.
WHAT THE WRAPPER DOES. The call is redirected to a 36-byte stub that converts as before, and on the
indefinite result substitutes the saturation value -- but only when the original double was
POSITIVE. __ftol2_sse returns 0x80000000 for negative overflow and for NaN as well, and saturating
those to +max would invent enormous damage out of a broken calculation. The sign is taken with FTST
before the conversion (C0 in the FPU status word) and stashed across the call:
fld st(0) / ftst / fnstsw ax / fstp st(0)   ; sign of the value, copy discarded
and ax, 0x0100 / push eax                   ; C0 = 'value < 0', stashed
call __ftol2_sse                            ; eax = (int)value
pop ecx / cmp eax, 0x80000000 / jne done
test ecx, ecx / jnz done                    ; negative or NaN -> leave it, old behaviour
mov eax, saturate_to
done: ret
eax/ecx are volatile across this helper's own convention, so using ecx is safe; the FPU copy is
pushed and popped so the stack depth is unchanged.
WHY NOT INT_MAX. Three modifiers run AFTER the conversion and at least one multiplies (the
job-change damage-up rate reaches 2.0x, and the level-gap revision scales too). Saturating at
0x7FFFFFFF would simply wrap again a few instructions later and land back on the clamp. 0x00FFFFFF
is ~16.7M: far above any real HP pool, and it survives an 8x downstream multiply inside int32.
Raise it with --set saturate_to=... if you want, but keep headroom for those multipliers.
WIRE WIDTHS, for choosing a value: melee is 'damage u16 @6' in SWING_DAMAGE, so anything at or
above 65535 shows as the u16 maximum there; skill damage carries 'hpchange u32 @4' and has room
for the full value. (Measured layouts, docs/COMBAT_BIBLE.md in ik-fiesta-bots.)
SIBLINGS. There are 209 __ftol2_sse call sites in the binary and most of them convert RATES and
STATS (roe_AC, roe_MinWC, roe_MaxWC, roe_HitRate, roe_CriticalRate, roe_TB, roe_MR). Saturating
those would be wrong -- they are small numbers and an indefinite there means a broken stat, not a
big hit. Only two sites convert a finished DAMAGE value into the int that gets returned, and both
have the same shape ('call __ftol2_sse' then 'mov [ebp-0x10], eax'):
0x506187  roe_CalcDamage            (+0x587)
0x504A27  roe_AttackPowerCalcDamage (+0x257)
Both are redirected here.
DELIBERATELY NOT PATCHED: 0x5046D8 in roe_GetAttackPower, which converts attack POWER rather than
damage. It could overflow by the same mechanism, but saturating it changes an input to the damage
formula instead of the result, which is a wider behaviour change than was asked for. Worth revisiting
if huge attack power turns out to be a real case.

new_section.name: .dmgfix
new_section.note: Executable. Must be materialised: code cannot live in a zero-fill BSS tail.

edits.why: roe_CalcDamage: redirect the double->int conversion at 0x506187 to the wrapper
roe_AttackPowerCalcDamage: same conversion at 0x504A27 -> the same wrapper
